title: Minimum Number of Work Sessions to Finish the Tasks
summary: Given an array of task durations and a session time limit, determine the minimum number of work sessions needed to complete all tasks.
statement: Given an array of task durations and a session time limit, determine the minimum number of work sessions needed to complete all tasks. Tasks must be finished within the same session if they are started, and tasks can be taken up immediately after finishing the previous one. Tasks can be completed in any order.
constraints: tasks has 1 through 14 positive durations, each no greater than session_time.
A session can contain any tasks whose total duration does not exceed session_time.
Return the fewest sessions needed to finish every task.
reference_solution:
def minimum_work_sessions(tasks, session_time):
    tasks = sorted(tasks, reverse=True)
    sessions = []
    best = len(tasks)
    def search(index):
        nonlocal best
        if len(sessions) >= best:
            return
        if index == len(tasks):
            best = len(sessions)
            return
        duration = tasks[index]
        tried = set()
        for position in range(len(sessions)):
            if sessions[position] in tried or sessions[position] + duration > session_time:
                continue
            tried.add(sessions[position])
            sessions[position] += duration
            search(index + 1)
            sessions[position] -= duration
        sessions.append(duration)
        search(index + 1)
        sessions.pop()
    search(0)
    return best

hints: This is bin packing over at most fourteen tasks, allowing exact search with strong pruning.
Place long tasks first; try each distinct current session load and also a new session, abandoning branches no better than the best.
Sort descending; recursively place task i in every fitting unique load or append a session.
Every legal assignment appears in a branch; equal-load symmetry and the incumbent bound remove only equivalent or non-improving branches.
